newsitem.title: EU: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR APR 2-DEC 31, 1997 (PAGE 1/9 - APRIL 2-15).
newsitem.headline: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR APR 2-DEC 31, 1997 (PAGE 1/9 - APRIL 2-15).

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
AMSTERDAM - The Netherlands hosts summit of European Union leaders (June 16-17).
MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9).
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg hosts summit of European Union leaders (December 12-13).
APRIL
BRUSSELS - Bosnian donor countries hold conference to discuss future of former Yugoslavia. (Date not fixed yet).
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 2
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Flynn green paper on new ways to organise work.
- Commissioner Kinnock communication on airport dangers.
- Commissioners Bangemann and Van Miert communication on shipbuilding policy - first reflections on future options.
BRUSSELS - Swedish Ministry of Environment holds seminar on "Chemicals, environment and human health" (1530/1330 GMT). Venue: Sweden's permanent representation to the EU, Square de Meeus 30.
THURSDAY, APRIL 3

DUBAI - The Dubai conference on the Euro-Arab peace process to further cooperation between two regions (To April 5). Main issues discussed are water resources management, energy management, high tech industrial cooperation and information technology, privatisation and private sector promotion. Contact: Sunil John, PanGulf Public Relations (9714) 219065.
FRIDAY, APRIL 4

NOORDWIJK, Netherlands - Informal ECOFIN Council (To April 6). (possibly) Discussions on regulations for EMU stability pact, legal framework for the euro and ERM 2. Ministers look at designs for euro coin ahead of formal decision by EU leaders in June.
SUNDAY, APRIL 6
MAASTRICHT - Informal Cultural Affairs Council (To April 8). Discussions focus on book prices and the future of public television.
MONDAY, APRIL 7
NOORDWIJK, Netherlands - EU-Rio Group meeting involving South American countries and Mexico, Panama, Trinidad, Tobago and Costa Rica (To April 8).
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To April 11).
BONN - European Commission hosts first annual electronic commerce conference "G7 - Global marketplace for SMEs project" (To April 9). Contact: Sandra Helms, Empirica GmbH (49) 228 985 3888.
SALZBURG - ACI Europe holds conference on airport development and evironment issues (To April 9). Contact: Yevgeny Pogorelov (322) 552 0982.
BERLIN - International European Training Centre holds seminar on "Building Europe: EU enlargement and deepening". Contact: International European Training Centre (33) 4 92 15 2121.
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 9
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts ministerial conference on social integration (To April 11).
THURSDAY, APRIL 10
LUXEMBOURG - Consumers Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Voluntary agreements as important instruments for consumer policy - Council resolution.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on injunctions for the protection of consumer interests.

- Proposal for an EP and Council directive amending directive 87/102/EEC (as amended by Directive 90/88/EEC) for the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning consumer credit.
- (possibly) Report of the Commission on the application of directive 87/012/EEC concerning consumer credit.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the sale of consumer goods and associated guarantees.

BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds annual banquet (1900/1800 GMT). European Commissioner Kinnock attends. Venue: Hilton Hotel. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce (322) 540 9030.
FRIDAY, APRIL 11
VENICE, Italy - First scientific congress to review measures taken by the EU to restore consumer confidence in beef after the mad cow crisis (To April 12).

LONDON - The Royal Institute of International Affairs holds conference on "Trade and environment: conflict or compatibility?". Sessions include: trade and environment after Singapore; trade versus environment - the evidence; industry concerns; resolving trade and environment disputes; the future. Speakers include: European Commissioner Brittan. Venue: Chatham House, 10 St James Square. Contact: Sharon Moore (44) 171 957 5700.
MONDAY, APRIL 14
LUXEMBOURG - Fisheries Council (To April 15).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Council decision on Multiannual Guidance Programmes (Structural arrangements for 1997-1999).
- (possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation laying down certain technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources.
- Proposal for a Council decision on a specific measure to encourage Italian fishermen to diversify out of certain fishing activities.
- (possibly) Communication from the Commission to Council and EP on fisheries agreements (Present situation and future prospects).
- (possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation allocating among Member States, for 1997, Community fish quotas of Atlanto-Scandian herring and horse mackerel.
- (possibly) Accession of Community to General Fisheries Council for the Mediterranean.
- (possibly) Consultations with Norway on a new management regime for North Sea herring.
- (possibly) Consultations with Norway on a new management regime for mackerel.
- Proposal for a Council regulation providing for the opening and management of autonomous Community tariff quotas for certain fisheries products (1997).
LEIDEN, Netherlands - The Philip Morris Institute (PMI) holds conference on "How much popular support is there for he EU?". Contact: PMI (322) 732 1156.
TUESDAY, APRIL 15

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds workshop on "Identifying the priorities for energy conservation" (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes: myths and realities in energy conservation: what is really needed; energy conservation in business: potentials and obstacles; the impacts of liberalisation on energy efficiency and renewables; integration of climate change objectives; how the necessary long-term consensus on climate change policy can be established. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

BRUSSELS - The European Energy Foundation holds dinner debate on "Medium and long term security of supply of oil and gas in Europe" (1900/1700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Europa. Contact: The European Energy Foundation (322) 773 9522.
VALETTA, Malta - EU and Mediterranean ministers attend Euro-Med conference in a follow-up to the 1995 Barcelona conference (To April 16). Commission clears merger concerning Birmingham airport
EUROPEAN COMMISSION PRESS RELEASE: IP/97/250
DOCUMENT DATE: MARCH 25, 1997
The Commission clears a merger concerning BIRMINGHAM
INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

The European Commission has authorised a joint venture through which the two companies which are active in the operation and management of Birmingham International Airport, Birmingham International Airport Ltd. and Eurohub (Birmingham) Ltd., will in the future be jointly controlled by the seven District Councils of the British West Midlands on the one hand and Aer Rianta International cpt and NatWest Ventures Ltd of the National Westminster Bank group on the other hand.
Birmingham Airport is one of the most important airports in the UK, 5th in terms of total passenger numbers and 3rd in terms of charter passengers.

Through the present operation the Districts, already shareholders in both companies, have brought in two new shareholders with experience in airport operation, Aer Rianta, and financial investment, NatWest, for the purpose of funding and developing a project to expand the Airport's terminal capacity to accommodate the expected doubling of the number of passengers by the year 2010.

In competition terms, the main consequence of the operation is that an important airport operator, Aer Rianta, will not only participate in the control of Birmingham Airport but will also contribute its advice and know-how to the new airport expansion project. However, Aer Rianta has no other airport operation and management activities in the UK, as its European airport activities are confined to Dublin, Shannon and Cork Airports in Ireland. Consequently, the European Commission has concluded that there is neither creation nor strengthening of a dominant position as a result of the proposed operation and has, therefore, decided not to oppose it. END OF DOCUMENT.
